title: 2027 Ford Maverick XL Goes Hybrid-Only, EcoBoost Gets More (and Less) Expensive

body_markdown:
Ford is rejiggering the Maverick range for the 2027 model year, according to a new report, and the changes will make the more powerful models—with the 2.0-liter EcoBoost turbo four—simultaneously cheaper and more expensive. The most affordable EcoBoost-powered Maverick will cost more in 2027 than it did in 2026, but the trims positioned near and at the top of the range will benefit from a four-digit price drop.


Citing internal order guide data,[CarsDirect](https://www.carsdirect.com/automotive-news/2027-ford-maverick-ecoboost-prices-cut-by-up-to-4-270?_cl=FcNUs1BdGjsbgbWQs9bgD8qu) reports that the EcoBoost-powered Maverick costs up to $4270 less in 2027 than it did for the 2026 model year. Ford is also reshuffling powertrain availability across the range, according to the report. Fewer trims will be available with the turbo 2.0-liter, because base (XL) and Lariat trims no longer offer it. Both trims will be available exclusively as hybrids for 2027.


The most affordable Maverick for 2027 remains the front-wheel-drive, hybrid XL, which starts at $28,145 excluding destination. That’s the same MSRP as the 2026 model, which is great news. If you want the EcoBoost powertrain, you’ll need to step up to the all-wheel-drive XLT, priced at $30,745 excluding destination. Axing the EcoBoost powertrain from the base XL trim effectively makes the 2.0-liter turbo-four $3600 more expensive than before.


With the XL and the Lariat out of the EcoBoost picture, the XLT, Lobo, and Tremor are the only trims available with the more powerful driveline. Pricing for the 2027 Lobo Standard starts at $32,155, which represents a $3775 drop compared to the 2026 model, while the 2027 Lobo High carries a base price of $37,155, a drop of $4270 over the 2026 model. The range-topping, off-road-focused[Tremor](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2023-ford-maverick-tremor-review-a-class-of-one/) will cost $37,155 as well for 2027, meaning it’s $3490 less than the 2026 model. Interestingly, the list of standard equipment remains the same. This isn’t a case of a car manufacturer stripping features from a model in order to advertise a more attractive base price.


Ford hasn’t commented on the report, and official information about the 2027 Ford Maverick hasn’t been released yet.


The unibody Maverick has stood proud as the most affordable truck on the American market since it made its debut for 2022, and it sounds like it will keep this positioning as it enters the 2027 model year. Soon, it won’t be the only Ford truck priced below $30,000, however. Earlier in 2026, Ford announced[a new electric truck called Fathom](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/getting-to-the-bottom-of-fords-28350-fathom/) that will start at $28,350 including destination.


Amazon-backed Slate wants a slice of this segment as well. Its first model is[a small, back-to-the-basics pickup](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/picture-car-confidential/picture-car-confidential-45-slate-first-drive/) whose base price will land in the vicinity of $25,000. The truck will be electric, and Slate plans to sell a $5000 kit that turns it into an SUV.
